items.title: From bag-loving monkeys to unrelenting umbrellas: Khyrunnisa's Happy Go Funny is hilarious
items.summary: Somehow, with the lamented disappearance of the cosy ways of the past–handwritten letters and coiling telephones–what has also gone missing is the easy humour one used to find in the most ordinary days of life. It needn’t be as momentous as a humiliating fall before an audience, but as simple as misreading someone’s warning of monkeys on the road as a reference to the noisy kids next door. Only, you need the right language to convey the humour of those very ordinary days, the ordinariness of it slightly disturbed by your tryst with a monkey or an umbrella that fails to close. Beloved writer of children’s books Khyrunnisa A comes both with the language and the timing you need to make humour work in her newest collection of essays, Happy Go Funny - The Lighter Moments of Life . In her third book for grown-ups, or rather for all age groups, it is mostly her choice of phrases that does the trick.
